metadata.case_name: Yugoslav Successors: Slovenia vs Croatia vs Serbia vs Bosnia-Herzegovina
metadata.author: transcribed from live/runs by expansion agent
metadata.key_test: P1 ordinal prediction at the violent end, and Safeguard A: Bosnia's post-Dayton governance scores partly reflect the Office of the High Representative's Bonn Powers, so measured capacity overstates indigenous P1.
metadata.notes: Breakup of Yugoslavia into 7 successor states via violent contested secession (engineered). Pre-event 1996, post-Dayton. These countries are NOT in the user M-score dataset; post-event trajectory is qualitative (EU accession milestones). 1996 pillar values are ordinal estimates; the one exact pre-event WGI figure recovered is Croatia's 1996 Rule-of-Law estimate of -0.67 (legacy WGI -2.5..+2.5 scale, all-time low) which is NOT placed in the 0-100 indicator slot to avoid scale-mixing. WGI 2025-anchored vintage caveat applies.

pre_event.event_description: Violent dissolution of Yugoslavia into 7 successor states (post-Dayton, 1996); divergent post-war trajectories.

data_sources.wgi: World Bank WGI via TheGlobalEconomy.com (1996, ordinal; Slovenia series avg ~1.02, 1998 max 1.26, legacy scale)

Slovenia.notes: 1996 estimate (ordinal): P1 high, balanced -> MI high (~0.45+), narrow spread. Regional leader; WGI Rule of Law ~+1.0 (legacy scale; series averaged ~1.02 with 1998 max 1.26) and Govt Effectiveness highest. HDI 1995 = 0.760; GDP per cap PPP 1996 highest by far; resource rents low; political stability high. Ordering P1: Slovenia >> Croatia > Serbia >= Bosnia. Pillar values are estimates, not exact 0-100 WGI; legacy-scale RoL figure not placed in indicator slot. WGI 2025-anchored vintage caveat applies.

data_sources.wgi: World Bank WGI via TheGlobalEconomy.com (Croatia 1996 Rule-of-Law estimate -0.67, its all-time low, legacy scale)

Croatia.notes: 1996 estimate (ordinal): P1 moderate-negative, recovering -> MI moderate-low, middle of the four. The one exact pre-event WGI figure recovered for the case: Croatia 1996 Rule of Law = -0.67 (its all-time low; legacy WGI -2.5..+2.5 scale) -- NOT placed in the 0-100 rule_of_law indicator slot to avoid scale-mixing. HDI 1995 medium band; GDP per cap PPP 1996 middle; resource rents low; political stability recovering. WGI 2025-anchored vintage caveat applies.

data_sources.wgi: World Bank WGI (1996, ordinal; exact 1996 estimate not isolated, clearly negative/bottom)

Serbia.notes: 1996 estimate (ordinal): P1 negative (~-1, not isolated), P4 sanctions-distorted -> MI low. WGI Rule of Law strongly negative; Govt Effectiveness negative. HDI 1995 = 0.674; GDP per cap PPP 1996 low (sanctions); resource rents low; political stability low (Milosevic). Held back by low P1 plus predatory/pariah status. Pillar values are estimates; exact 1996 WGI not isolated (reported missing, not interpolated). WGI 2025-anchored vintage caveat applies.

context.admin_details: Post-Dayton Office of the High Representative (OHR) holds 'Bonn Powers' -- the power to impose laws and remove elected officials. WGI partly measures international-administrator competence, not indigenous capacity (Safeguard A).
context.backstop_details: OHR international administration under the Dayton Agreement.

data_sources.wgi: World Bank WGI (1996, ordinal; exact 1996 estimate not isolated, bottom/administrator-driven)

Bosnia-Herzegovina.notes: 1996 estimate (ordinal): P1 bottom (and externally administered), P5 floor -> MI lowest; widest vulnerability. Safeguard A applied: discount measured capacity because WGI reflects the OHR administrator overlay (Bonn Powers), so indigenous P1 is lower than measured. WGI Rule of Law bottom (not isolated; OHR overlay); Govt Effectiveness bottom/administrator-driven. HDI 1995 not reported (war); GDP per cap PPP 1996 lowest (war-devastated); resource rents low; political stability very low (post-war). Pillar values are estimates; exact 1996 WGI not isolated (reported missing, not interpolated). WGI 2025-anchored vintage caveat applies.

a_trajectory_ranking.prediction: Four-way ordinal: Slovenia > Croatia > Serbia > Bosnia.
a_trajectory_ranking.basis: P1 ordering Slovenia >> Croatia > Serbia >= Bosnia, with Bosnia's measured capacity discounted under Safeguard A.
a_trajectory_ranking.falsification_condition: Any lower-P1 successor out-trajectories a higher-P1 one (e.g., Bosnia surpasses Slovenia).

b_violence.prediction: Violence (retroactive) concentrated where pre-war institutional profile was weakest / ethnic-factional fragility highest (Bosnia and Serbia/FRY), not in Slovenia (10-day war, minimal deaths).
b_violence.agency_note: Mod8: this predicts RISK, not AGENCY
b_violence.falsification_condition: Severe violence concentrated in the highest-P1 successor (Slovenia).

c_convergence.prediction: Divergence (Slovenia converges to EU core; Bosnia diverges downward).
c_convergence.basis: Wide pre-event P1 spread across the four.
c_convergence.falsification_condition: Convergence of outcomes across the four successors.

d_failure_dimension.prediction: Slovenia succeeds on P1; Bosnia fails on indigenous P1 + stability; Serbia held back by P1 + predatory/pariah status; Croatia mid.
d_failure_dimension.note: Most exposed to post-hoc coding bias
d_failure_dimension.falsification_condition: Outcomes driven by a non-P1 dimension.

e_fragment_count.prediction: 7 successors = engineered (violent contested secession, not organic state formation).

g_suppression_mechanism.classification: Military suppression: the wars were resolved by force/partition (Croatia's Operation Storm, Dayton's military annexes, NATO).
g_suppression_mechanism.falsification_condition: Resolution achieved by legal/institutional rather than military means.

time_points: qualitative trajectory (not in user M-score dataset)

Slovenia.outcome_summary: Best trajectory: EU 2004, eurozone 2007; 'very high human development' (HDI 0.760 -> 0.918, 1995 -> 2021).

Serbia.outcome_summary: Stalled: EU candidate 2012, negotiations 2014, still not a member; democratic backsliding.

Bosnia-Herzegovina.outcome_summary: Worst trajectory: EU candidate only 2022, negotiations conditionally opened March 2024; still under OHR; Republika Srpska secession threats (Dodik, 2025).

a_trajectory.evidence: EU accession dates map exactly: Slovenia 2004 > Croatia 2013 > Serbia candidate > Bosnia candidate-last.
a_trajectory.explanation: Four-way P1 ordering reproduced the four-way outcome ordering.

b_violence.evidence: Institutional weakness is consistent with the violence locus, but the 1996 data is post-war; cannot fully separate pre-war P1 from war damage.
b_violence.explanation: Direction correct (violence concentrated in low-P1 Bosnia/Serbia) but coded conservatively because 1996 measures are post-war.

c_convergence.evidence: Slovenia converged to EU core while Bosnia diverged downward.
c_convergence.explanation: Outcomes diverged across the spread as predicted.

d_failure_dimension.evidence: CONFIRMED for Slovenia/Bosnia poles; PARTIAL for Serbia/Croatia middle.
d_failure_dimension.explanation: The P1-failure dimension holds cleanly at the poles but is mixed for the middle two.

f_reversal_risk.explanation: No reversal-risk (Safeguard C) prediction was made for this case.

g_suppression.evidence: Tier 1 military suppression: Croatia's Operation Storm, Dayton's military annexes, NATO.
g_suppression.explanation: The wars were resolved by force/partition, matching the Tier 1 classification.

h_turbulence.explanation: No sub-state turbulence (Safeguard F) prediction was made for this case.

result_coding_reference.CONFIRMED: Prediction matched outcome on the specific dimension predicted
result_coding_reference.PARTIALLY_CONFIRMED: Direction correct but magnitude, form, or timing significantly different
result_coding_reference.NOT_APPLICABLE: Prediction type not relevant to this case
result_coding_reference.coding_rule: When ambiguous between confirmed and partial, code PARTIAL. When ambiguous between partial and falsified, code PARTIAL but note ambiguity.

analysis.overall_assessment: Confirms the framework at the violent end of the spectrum. Four-way ordering, divergence, engineered count, and Tier 1 military suppression all CONFIRMED; violence and failure-dimension PARTIALLY CONFIRMED due to post-war measurement and mixed middle. Safeguard A is essential -- without it Bosnia's OHR-inflated governance scores would overstate indigenous capacity and weaken the prediction.
safeguards_triggered: A (Bosnia under OHR/Dayton -- measured > actual capacity)
G (military suppression during the wars -- Tier 1)
analysis.what_this_case_uniquely_reveals: Validates the framework's handling of externally administered states (Safeguard A). The violence-severity end is anchored by the RDC Sarajevo 'Bosnian Book of the Dead': 97,207 confirmed named dead/missing (66.2% Bosniak, 25.4% Serb, 7.8% Croat), 'the largest existing database on Bosnian war victims' (Ewa Tabeau, ICTY); the wider Yugoslav Wars killed at least 130,000 (Humanitarian Law Center) to 140,000 (ICTJ).
proposed_framework_modifications: Codify Safeguard A: if an OHR-type body holds binding legislative power (Bonn Powers), flag indigenous P1 as 'measured > actual.'
analysis.baseline_impact: None degrading; supports keeping Safeguard A. No 20-case baseline-breaking modification proposed.
